title: Frame Language term registry
description: The canonical machine-readable Frame 1 vocabulary registry of Dimensional Frame Language: each entry names a Frame 1 term (one that imports a structural assumption independently of intent) and the Frame 2 replacement that carries the inheritance intact, with the strengthened form, the procedure, and what the Frame 1 term forecloses. A controlled vocabulary published as a code-system; the skill, the MCP server, and the analyzer derive their watchlists from this one source.

term.description: The Frame 1 term this entry is about.

frame.description: The frame the term speaks from. Registry entries are Frame 1 terms.

imports.description: The structural assumption the term imports independently of the author's intent.

frame_2_replacement.description: One or more Frame 2 terms that name the structural condition the Frame 1 term was suppressing. May be empty where no replacement has been settled.

strengthened_form.description: The replacement rendered with the suppressed mechanism added back, so the correct replacement is not weaker than the term it replaces.

procedure.description: The named procedure for handling the term (for example plain-english, technical-corpus, relational-inversion).

forecloses.description: The structural requirement the Frame 1 term forecloses by hiding it.

slippage_note.description: Why a plausible reform reading of the term does not change its structural direction.

primitive_anchors.description: The corpus primitives the replacement anchors to, where any exist.

common_phrasings.description: Recurring Frame 1 phrasings paired with their Frame 2 renderings.

admissibility_note.description: A note on when the term is admissible despite being Frame 1 (for example when a document is analyzing a Frame 1 structure and names it as such).

sources.description: The prior encodings this entry was reconciled from: the Frame Language Grammar, the MCP server watchlist, the analyzer term registry.
